questions.question: Which correction fixes the spelling in: "qize is not qualified"?
options: A. Quiz is not qualified.
B. Qize is not qualified.
C. Quize is not qualified.
D. The qize is not qualify.
questions.explanation: Spell "quiz" correctly. "Qualified" is already correct as an adjective meaning "up to standard."

questions.question: Which is the correct capitalization for: "should I downgrade it to a lower version?"
options: A. Should I downgrade it to a lower version?
B. should I downgrade it to a lower version?
C. Should i downgrade it to a lower version?
D. Should I Downgrade It To A Lower Version?
questions.explanation: Capitalize the first word of a sentence and the pronoun "I". Do not capitalize every word.

questions.question: In "I set the log level to info, check what is consuming the proxy traffic", what is the best fix?
options: A. I set the log level to info check what is consuming the proxy traffic
B. I set the log level to info. Check what is consuming the proxy traffic.
C. I set the log level to info, checking what is consuming the proxy traffic.
D. I set the log level to info and check what consuming proxy traffic.
questions.explanation: Two separate actions need a period or semicolon. "Check what is consuming the proxy traffic" is a clear imperative follow-up.

questions.question: What does "high energy impact" most likely refer to when asking about ClashX Meta?
options: A. The proxy uses too much network bandwidth
B. The app drains battery or uses excessive CPU on macOS
C. The proxy rules consume too much disk space
D. The DNS resolution is slower than expected
questions.explanation: On macOS, "energy impact" refers to battery and CPU usage reported in Activity Monitor, not network throughput.

questions.question: Which question best asks whether a streaming service routes through a proxy?
options: A. Does iqiyi use the proxy?
B. Is iqiyi using proxy?
C. Does iqiyi uses the proxy?
D. iqiyi use proxy?
questions.explanation: "Does [service] use the proxy?" is the natural form. Option C has a subject-verb agreement error; B omits "the."

questions.question: In a debugging context, what does "consuming the proxy traffic" mean?
options: A. Deleting proxy configuration files
B. Using bandwidth or connections through the proxy
C. Blocking all outbound network requests
D. Encrypting traffic before it reaches the proxy
questions.explanation: "Consuming proxy traffic" means an app or process is actively sending data through the proxy, using its bandwidth.

questions.question: Translate into natural technical English: "查一下什么东西有跑了一个G的流量"
questions.modelAnswer: Check what has used about 1 GB of data/traffic.
questions.explanation: "1 G" means roughly one gigabyte of data. "What has used" or "what is using" captures 什么东西有跑了 in a network-monitoring context.

questions.question: Translate into natural technical English: "gpt正在跑什么流量"
questions.explanation: Keep it short and direct. "What traffic is [app] using?" is standard when investigating which connections an app makes.

questions.question: Evaluate and improve if needed: "Get the entire flow working end-to-end."
questions.modelAnswer: Get the entire flow working end to end.
questions.explanation: The phrase is already natural. "End to end" as an adverb often appears without hyphens; "end-to-end" is also acceptable as a compound modifier before a noun.

questions.question: Rewrite as a clear bug report: "The tts output is missing the first word in the translation panel"
questions.modelAnswer: The TTS output is missing the first word in the translation panel.
questions.explanation: Capitalize the acronym TTS (text-to-speech). The sentence structure is otherwise clear — state what is broken, where, and what is missing.
